answer: Drainage beats floodlights. Karst aquifers surface at a few springs, so decisions form in small random shards that reshuffle weekly; a quorum of strangers ratifies each act. To steer one spring a clone herd must win every shard at once, buying a spread of stakes that vanishes into the rock before surfacing. No haven hides an operator: quartz-clock epochs re-deal the map before any cell learns where it must be heavy.
